correctness.rationale: Prime-order descent forces least divisor 3 and prefix support; each valuation is established by LTE at odd primes and 3. Zsigmondy for \(10^{3^a}-1\) supplies distinct new primes. A real primitive mod-40 quadratic character captures all supported primes. The exact Euler-factor identity and classical Selberg–Delange yield the constant and an upper bound for lengths. Standalone finite checker reports 120000 exact comparisons, 27 solutions and 4 distinct primitive seeds; finite checks are not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The result classifies every self-dividing digit length via finite prime-prefix order tests, solves natural exact two-prime-support subfamilies with infinitely many distinct primes, and obtains a genuinely quantitative zero-density bound on length indices. These are motivated by OEIS A095250 and the published repdigit Niven question. The density claim is correctly one-sided and does not conflate repunit-value sparsity with length-index sparsity.
